newsitem.title: UK: BOE says considering gilt price decimilisation.
newsitem.headline: BOE says considering gilt price decimilisation.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Monday it was looking at the subject of decimilisation of gilt market prices and that the matter would be included in its next quarterly review on European monetary union in April,
"It is an issue which we have been looking at," a Bank official told Reuters. "The next quarterly report (on monetary union) will contain something on it."
The remarks followed comments on gilt pricing methods by an International Securities Market Association executive at a conferrence on European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) on Monday.
John Dowsett, ISMA board member and chairman of its market practices committee, said he hoped the current method of quoting gilt prices would change.

"I think fractions are about to disappear. I certainly hope so. I think the Bank of England is shortly going to come out with a plan to change the way the gilt market is quoted to decimals," he told delegates at the conference.
Bond markets throughout Europe, except for Britain, quote bond and bond futures prices in basis points. Britain's gilt market, like the U.S. Treasuries market, quotes debt prices in 32nds.
The Bank of England official was unable to specify the exact date on which the next EMU review would be released.
